parameter_semantics: every strength is a SIMULATED INTERVENTION STRENGTH — a perturbation magnitude applied to the model's input state. It is NOT a real-world effectiveness, efficacy or success rate.

scope.timesteps_modified: the FINAL timestep only (the current state)
scope.why: the defender acts NOW; earlier timesteps are OBSERVED HISTORY and rewriting them would fabricate a past that did not happen
scope.rows_preserved_verbatim: base rows 0..8 and relative-change rows 0..8, copied from the observed tensor
scope.relative_change_row_0: PRESERVED, never regenerated — these are sliding windows, so row 0 was computed against the window before the sequence begins and is not recomputable from inside it
scope.consequence: projected changes are modest by construction: the V4 encoder is an LSTM over ten windows, so one perturbed window has limited leverage. This is a property of the model being probed, reported rather than tuned away.

verified_identities.fwd_packet_ratio + bwd_packet_ratio == 1: holds to 1.9e-08 — float32 storage precision on a quantity of order 1.0
verified_identities.fwd_byte_ratio + bwd_byte_ratio: NOT 1 (measured mean 0.663) — so no sum constraint is imposed and the byte ratios are left unchanged

required: This simulator does not estimate causal real-world effectiveness. It applies a defined state perturbation and rolls the frozen World Model forward.
forbidden: Defense will reduce the attack by X%

RATE_LIMIT.display: Defend now — uniform traffic rate limit
RATE_LIMIT.concept: Throttle the volume of traffic crossing the monitored boundary by the simulated strength, without selecting particular destinations or ports.
RATE_LIMIT.parameter: simulated intervention strength (fraction of volume withheld), in [0, 1]
RATE_LIMIT.justification: flow_count, total_packets and total_bytes are the three underlying volume quantities in the frozen contract, and the log / rate features are exact derivations of them (identities verified to 1e-7 on the frozen substrate). A rate limit reduces the underlying quantities, so every derived feature must move with them. Nothing outside that derivation chain is touched.

unchanged.syn_rate: per-flow flag presence / packets, averaged over flows. Dropping or throttling whole flows leaves the per-flow statistic's distribution unchanged in expectation; no signed change is derivable from the feature definition.
unchanged.rst_rate: as syn_rate. (A real block would likely RAISE rst_rate, but neither the magnitude nor the flow-accounting consequence is derivable from the contract, so it is not invented.)
unchanged.mean_pkt_len: mean over flows of each flow's mean packet length. A uniform volume reduction does not change the mean-of-per-flow-means in expectation.
unchanged.std_pkt_len: mean over flows of each flow's packet-length std; same argument as mean_pkt_len.
unchanged.log_mean_flow_duration: a rate limit or block plausibly changes flow lifetimes, but neither the sign nor the magnitude follows from the feature definition. Left unchanged rather than guessed.
unchanged.log_mean_fwd_iat: as log_mean_flow_duration (a rate limit would plausibly INCREASE inter-arrival time, but by an amount the contract does not determine).
unchanged.fwd_packet_ratio: a ratio, invariant to uniform volume scaling. Also constrained by the measured identity fwd_packet_ratio + bwd_packet_ratio == 1.0 (to float32 precision), which leaving both unchanged preserves.
unchanged.fwd_byte_ratio: a ratio, invariant to uniform volume scaling. NOTE the byte ratios do NOT sum to 1 (measured mean 0.663), so no coupled redistribution can be defined for them and none is attempted.
unchanged.mean_down_up_ratio: an integer-valued per-flow ratio, averaged. Not derivably changed by uniform volume scaling.
unchanged.unique_protocols: a count of distinct protocols. Throttling volume does not remove a protocol from the window.
unchanged.protocol_entropy: Shannon entropy over protocol counts; unchanged for the same reason as unique_protocols.
unchanged.log_unique_dst_ports: throttling volume does not remove a destination port from the window

RESTRICT_EGRESS.display: Block C2 / restrict egress — destination allow-listing
RESTRICT_EGRESS.concept: Block a fraction of the distinct outbound destination ports observed in the current window, as an egress allow-list would.
RESTRICT_EGRESS.parameter: simulated intervention strength (fraction of distinct destination ports blocked), in [0, 1]
transformation: then the same coupled volume reduction as RATE_LIMIT
RESTRICT_EGRESS.justification: Two consequences follow from the contract's own definitions. log_unique_dst_ports is log1p(nunique of Dst Port), so blocking a fraction of destinations reduces the count directly. dst_port_entropy is Shannon entropy over the destination-port counts, which is bounded above by log2 of the support size; rescaling by the ratio of ceilings shrinks entropy with its bound and preserves the measured invariant entropy <= log2(nunique) (0 violations on the frozen substrate). Volume falls too, on the first-order assumption that blocked destinations carry a proportional share of the window's flows. Direction ratios are NOT shifted because 'forward' is the direction of a flow's first packet, so egress blocking removes whole flows rather than re-balancing surviving ones.
